mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer confidence and spending, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is below 5% but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 20-day periods, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5% but SPX returns are positive in more than 50% of the next 20-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) is increasing, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE is below 5% and PAYEMS is increasing but SPX returns are negative in more than 30% of the next 60-day periods, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) leads to higher borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% but SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of the next 20-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is positive but SPX returns are negative in more than 35% of the next 60-day periods, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 200 indicates increasing inflation, which may lead to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL exceeds 200 but SPX returns are positive in more than 45% of the next 20-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP (GDPC1) is growing and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is low, it indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is positive and UNRATE is below 5% but SPX returns are negative in more than 30% of the next 60-day periods, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) during an economic expansion indicates strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but SPX returns are negative in more than 35% of the next 60-day periods, the hypothesis is falsified.
